label: rem:q-clt-jsj-mass-scaling
title: q-CLT / JSJ volume scaling for heavy isotopes
html:
Remark. q-CLT / JSJ volume scaling for heavy isotopes

When modeling the macroscopic atomic mass of heavy isotopes up to Oganesson (A=294), evaluating the absolute topological Hecke trace of the A-nucleon knot becomes computationally intractable. The Jaco–Shalen–Johannson (JSJ) decomposition glues the atomic knot complement along essential (inter-nucleon) tori, and hyperbolic volume is additive under torus gluing. The leading mass term is therefore volume-additive — linear in the nucleon counts:

\mathfrak{m}_{\text{qCLT,lead}}(Z, N) = Z\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}.

Accordingly we partition the absolute mass prediction into two computational channels:

  1. m_symbolic: the exact closed-form evaluation of the Hecke matrix traces, computationally constrained to light isotopes (A \le 8).
  2. m_qCLT_approx: the JSJ-additive estimator Z\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - B(Z,N), where B is the binding energy (the \Delta_\lambda correction).

The additive structure is exact: the inter-nucleon tori make the volume — hence the leading mass term — linear in (Z,N). The absolute prediction depends on two residuals: the binding fraction B/\mathfrak{m} (which plateaus near 0.9\% under nuclear saturation, so it does not vanish for heavy A) and the nucleon-mass gap. The nucleon-mass gap is +2.89\% in the proved pipeline (the production linking weight); the derived, no-fit spectral-phase correction \theta/(8\hbar_q^2)\approx 0.9711 reduces it \sim 35\times to -819 ppm, but is exploratory and not part of the production route (its "why \theta/(8\hbar_q^2)" step is an unproved Lean stub). Validated on the three light compound nuclei where B is available (D, T, {}^3\mathrm{He}), the binding-corrected channel reproduces the CODATA atomic mass to within the nucleon-mass gap, uniformly across isotopes — production residual \approx 2.89\% (cross-isotope spread 0.014\%), spectral residual \approx -800 ppm. The uniformity is the signature that the additive structure is sound; the asymptotic claim is about the linear structure, not absolute exactness. See the computational witness m-qclt-approx.witness.json.

The binding B admits two evaluations in this channel: the framework's per-isotope \Delta_\lambda prediction, and a self-contained factorized q-CLT binding B = \alpha \sum_i \ln\lvert V_i\rvert, with the derived scale \alpha = \mathfrak{m}_e/\!\left(q_0(q_0-1)\right) (fixed by q_0 and the electron mass alone — not Q_\beta, not a fit) and each V_i the Markov-trace ratio of a two-nucleon sub-braid for one bond type (p–p, p–n, n–n). Because the n–n bond is more suppressing than the p–p bond, this form resolves the {}^3\mathrm{H}/{}^3\mathrm{He} isospin splitting — which the isospin-blind leading term cannot — to within 1.1\times of the AME binding energy with no fit. The bond-count scaling (chain versus all-pairs) is a modeling choice rather than a derived quantity, and A \ge 4 undershoots, so this remains a structural estimator: the absolute mass still carries the nucleon-mass gap above. The binding-form diagram is given in the standard-part map appendix.
